facts.text: Mound takes its name from a prominent prehistoric Native American earthen mound that once marked the original settlement site.
The Vicksburg, Shreveport and Texas Railroad reached a terminus at Tallulah Station in 1857, spurring cotton trade and settlement growth.
The mound, like many in the Delta, was built by indigenous peoples for ceremonial or residential purposes, possibly linked to Poverty Point culture.
The Great Mississippi Flood of 1927 inundated Madison Parish, severely affecting Mound and surrounding communities.
Mound’s early 20th‑century economy hinged on agriculture, timber harvesting, and a nearby sawmill that supported a general store and hotel.
Mound lies just two miles south of the Mississippi River, placing it within the river’s floodplain.
